docs.title: GitHub API Documentation (Basic Guide)
docs.text:
Welcome to this beginner-friendly documentation for the GitHub REST API.

This guide is created by a technical writer who is not a developer – and that's the point! If you're curious about APIs but don't know where to start, you're in the right place.

docs.title: What is an API?
docs.text: An API (Application Programming Interface) allows different programs to talk to each other. In this case, GitHub provides a set of URLs you can send requests to in order to get information about repositories, issues, users, and more.

docs.title: What does it mean to 'interact with the GitHub API using HTTP requests'?
docs.text:
It means you can use tools like your browser, terminal, or Postman to send messages to GitHub and get responses. These messages follow a specific format using URLs and often include tokens (like passwords) to authenticate.

Example request: 

GET https://api.github.com/users/octocat

This would return data about the user "octocat".

docs.title: Why this guide?
docs.text: This documentation was written with clarity and simplicity in mind. It's for anyone who wants to understand the basics of APIs without being overwhelmed by code.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: To use the GitHub API, you'll need to authenticate.

docs.title: Types of Authentication
docs.text:
• Personal Access Tokens (PATs): Used in place of a password for Git operations.
  • OAuth Apps: Applications that access user data on GitHub.
  • GitHub Apps: Fine-grained control over API access.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Go to your GitHub Developer Settings.
  2. Click Generate new token.
  3. Choose scopes depending on your needs.
  4. Copy the token and store it securely.

🔒 Never share your token publicly.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text: Issues are used to track tasks, bugs, and feature requests.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: Repositories are where your project's files and history are stored.

docs.title: Common API Endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /user/repos: List your repositories
  • POST /user/repos: Create a new repository

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -H "Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN" \
     https://api.github.com/user/repos

This will list your repositories.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: User-related endpoints help you fetch GitHub profile information.

docs.title: Key Endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /users/:username: Get a user
  • GET /user: Get the authenticated user

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl https://api.github.com/users/octocat

This will return the public profile of Octocat.
